## §3 Discovery

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `discovery.well-known` A Company publishes its `poppy.json` document at `https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json` over HTTPS, where `{domain}` is the Company's domain or a subdomain it controls. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L9) | MUST | company | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| – | `discovery.redirect` The well-known URL may redirect, including to another host. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L10) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `discovery.redirect-https` Personal Agents follow redirects, and every redirect is to an HTTPS URL. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L11) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.final-path` Personal Agents use the document only when the last URL's path is exactly `/.well-known/poppy.json` and it has no query. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L12) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.cache` Personal Agents cache the document according to its HTTP caching headers. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L13) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.two-way` Before using a document, the Personal Agent checks that `organization.domain` is the host that served it, and that the issuer's metadata has the same `issuer` and lists `https://{organization.domain}` in `protected_resources`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L14) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `discovery.https` Every URL the protocol defines or exchanges is an HTTPS URL; Personal Agents don't use a URL from a Company with another scheme, and Companies reject one from a Personal Agent. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L15) | MUST | both | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| → | `discovery.redirect-secrets` When a protocol endpoint, API, or conversation, feedback or extension endpoint answers with a redirect, the Personal Agent does not send a token, DPoP Proof, assertion or credentials to the new URL. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L16) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `discovery.private-addresses` Personal Agents and Companies do not connect to a loopback, private or link-local address for a URL the other party gave them, unless configured to on purpose. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L17) | MUST NOT | both | `identity/private-agent-urls` |

## §3.2 OAuth server

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `issuer.shared` Several domains may name the same issuer, and they are then one Company sharing User IDs, Sessions and Account Tokens. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L52) | MAY | company |  |
| ✎ | `issuer.same-auth` Documents on several domains that name the same issuer have the same `auth`. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L53) | MUST | company | _one definePoppyseed serves every domain of a Company, so each document's auth comes from the same config_ |
| ✎ | `issuer.one-company` An issuer represents exactly one Company, and a provider that hosts several Companies gives each its own issuer, even on shared servers. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L54) | MUST | company | _each definePoppyseed is one Company, whose issuer is its own baseUrl; a provider runs one per Company_ |
| ✓ | `issuer.metadata` The issuer publishes OAuth Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414) at the URL RFC 8414 defines, and its `protected_resources` lists `https://{domain}`, scheme and host only, for every domain whose `poppy.json` names the issuer. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L55) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| → | `issuer.agent-check` Before using a Company's `poppy.json`, the Personal Agent checks that the metadata `issuer` matches `auth.issuer` character for character, and that `protected_resources` includes `https://{organization.domain}`, comparing exactly except for the case of the host. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L56) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `issuer.endpoints` The metadata has `token_endpoint`, `revocation_endpoint` and `grant_types_supported`, plus `authorization_endpoint` when `grant_types_supported` includes `authorization_code` and `device_authorization_endpoint` when it includes the device code grant. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L57) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| ✓ | `issuer.grant-types` `grant_types_supported` includes the JWT bearer grant and `refresh_token`, and the token exchange grant if the Company lists an MCP server that doesn't support DPoP. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L58) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| ✓ | `issuer.scopes-supported` A Company that offers any type of sign-in lists `scopes_supported`, with every account scope a Personal Agent can request. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L59) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| – | `issuer.hidden-scopes` `scopes_supported` may leave out scopes the Company doesn't offer Personal Agents. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L60) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `issuer.es256` Companies accept DPoP Proofs signed with `ES256`, and a `dpop_signing_alg_values_supported` they list includes `ES256`. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L61) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| → | `issuer.agent-alg` Personal Agents sign DPoP Proofs with `ES256` or an algorithm from `dpop_signing_alg_values_supported`. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L62) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `issuer.extra-fields` The metadata may have other fields, which Personal Agents ignore. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L63) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `issuer.cache` Personal Agents cache the metadata according to its HTTP caching headers. [↗](pap-0.3/03-discovery.md#L64) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.1 Agent identity

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `identity.client-id-url` A Personal Agent's `client_id` is an HTTPS URL that returns its client metadata document. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L33) | MUST | both | `identity/client-id-is-url` |
| ✓ | `identity.client-id-matches` `client_id` in the metadata document equals the URL the document was fetched from. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L34) | MUST | both | `identity/client-id-must-match` |
| ✓ | `identity.same-domain` `jwks_uri` and every entry in `redirect_uris` are HTTPS URLs on the same domain as `client_id`, and the key set contains only public keys. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L35) | MUST | both | `identity/keys-same-domain` |
| ✓ | `identity.private-key-jwt` The Personal Agent authenticates at the token endpoint with a client assertion signed by a key from `jwks_uri` (`private_key_jwt`, RFC 7523); its DPoP keys are separate and unpublished. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L36) | MUST | both | `identity/client-auth-required`<br>`identity/client-assertion-claims`<br>`identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| ✓ | `identity.client-assertion-aud` The client assertion's `aud` is the Company's `auth.issuer` as a single string, and Companies reject any other `aud`, compared character for character, including their token endpoint URL. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L37) | MUST | both | `identity/client-assertion-claims` |
| ✓ | `identity.client-assertion-replay` The client assertion follows the Session assertion's rules for `iat`, `exp` and `jti`, so the Company rejects a reused `jti` from the same `client_id` until it expires. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L38) | MUST | company | `identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| – | `identity.registration` Companies may require Personal Agents to register ahead of time. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L39) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `identity.unregistered` A Company that requires registration rejects an unregistered Personal Agent with `invalid_client` (HTTP 401) when it starts a Session. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L40) | MUST | company | `identity/unregistered` |
| – | `identity.allow-block` Companies may keep allowlists or blocklists of Personal Agents by `client_id`, and may revoke a `client_id` that misuses the protocol. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L41) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `identity.rate-limit` Companies may rate-limit Session creation by `client_id`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L42) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `identity.new-client-limit` A Company that doesn't require registration may limit how many new `client_id` values it accepts. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L43) | MAY | company |  |

## §4.2 Starting a Session

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `sessions.user-id-stable` The Personal Agent gives each of its Users a stable User ID for each Company, where a Company is identified by its `auth.issuer`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.user-id-no-pii` A User ID does not contain or derive from personal information, such as an email address, phone number or name, even with a keyed hash. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L61) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.anonymous-no-sign-in` A Personal Agent does not sign in with a Session that uses an anonymous browsing User ID. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L62) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.user-id-confidential` The Personal Agent keeps the mapping of each User's IDs across Companies confidential, never publishing it or sharing it with third parties other than service providers acting for it. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L63) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `sessions.jwt-bearer` A Session starts with the JWT bearer grant at `token_endpoint`: a short-lived assertion signed with a key from `jwks_uri`, with `iss` the `client_id`, `sub` the User ID, `aud` the `auth.issuer` as a single string, `iat`, `exp`, and a `jti` of at least 128 random bits, plus the client assertion and a DPoP Proof signed with a new Session Key. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L64) | MUST | both | `sessions/start-signed-out`<br>`sessions/assertion-aud`<br>`dpop/required` |
| ✓ | `sessions.assertion-aud` The Company rejects a Session assertion whose `aud` is anything but its `auth.issuer`, compared character for character. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L65) | MUST | company | `sessions/assertion-aud` |
| → | `sessions.assertion-lifetime` A Session assertion's `exp` is at most five minutes after `iat`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L66) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `sessions.verify-assertions` The Company verifies both assertions against the Personal Agent's `jwks_uri`, checks that the assertion's `iss` is the authenticated `client_id`, and rejects a `jti` it has already seen from the same `client_id` until the assertion expires. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L67) | MUST | company | `identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| ✓ | `sessions.response` The token response carries `access_token`, `token_type` `DPoP` and `expires_in`, and no `scope`, because a Session started with the assertion is signed out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L68) | MUST | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.expires-in` `expires_in` is greater than 0. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L69) | MUST | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.token-hours` Session Tokens last hours, not days. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L70) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/start-signed-out` |
| ✓ | `sessions.renew-same-owner` On renewal the Company finds the Session by the proof's key, checks that it belongs to the same `client_id` and User ID as the assertion, and returns `invalid_grant` for a key that names a Session of a different `client_id` or User ID. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L71) | MUST | company | `sessions/renew-same-owner` |
| ✓ | `sessions.remember-ended` A Company remembers the keys of the Sessions it ended, for as long as it chooses, and rejects them with `invalid_grant`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L72) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/ended-session` |
| → | `sessions.ended-key` After `invalid_grant` on a Session Key, the Personal Agent does not use that key again. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L73) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.renewal-may-restart` The Personal Agent is prepared for a renewal to start a new Session. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L74) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.opaque-tokens` Personal Agents do not depend on the contents of Session Tokens. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L75) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `sessions.embedded-credentials` A Company may include its own Session credentials in a token so its existing systems can read them. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L76) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `sessions.embedded-encrypted` A Company that includes its own Session credentials in a token encrypts the token. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L77) | MUST | company | `sessions/token-opaque` |
| ✓ | `sessions.errors` Token endpoint errors use the OAuth error response: `invalid_client` 401, `invalid_grant` 400, `account_mismatch` 400, `invalid_target` 400, `invalid_dpop_proof` and `use_dpop_nonce` 400, `extension_required` 403, `rate_limited` 429 with `Retry-After`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L78) | MUST | company | `sessions/renew-same-owner`<br>`dpop/required` |

## §4.3 Using Session Tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tokens.dpop-scheme` API calls and conversations carry the Session Token in the `Authorization` header with the `DPoP` scheme, together with a DPoP Proof. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L87) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `dpop.key-per-session` The Personal Agent creates a new key pair for each Session, its Session Key, and uses it for no other Session. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L88) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `dpop.session-key-names` Every token request for a Session carries a proof signed with its Session Key, whose JWK thumbprint names the Session; a Session can't change its key. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L89) | MUST | both | `sessions/renew-same-owner` |
| ✓ | `dpop.proof-claims` A proof has `jti`, `htm` and `htu` (the request's method and URL without the query or fragment), `iat`, `ath` (the SHA-256 hash of the Session Token, absent at the token endpoint and in a browser-session form), and `nonce` when required. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L90) | MUST | both | `dpop/htu` |
| ✓ | `dpop.bind` When the Company issues a Session Token, it binds the token to the key in that request's proof. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L91) | MUST | company | `dpop/api-binding` |
| ✓ | `dpop.verify` The Company validates every proof as RFC 9449 §4.3 describes: exactly one `DPoP` header holding a well-formed JWT, `typ` `dpop+jwt`, an asymmetric `alg` it accepts and never `none`, a `jwk` with no private key, a signature that verifies with it, matching `htm` and `htu`, made within its acceptance window, a matching `nonce` when it requires one, and on requests with a Session Token the bound key and a matching `ath`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L92) | MUST | company | `dpop/replay`<br>`dpop/htu`<br>`dpop/htm`<br>`dpop/iat-window`<br>`dpop/signature`<br>`dpop/jti-entropy`<br>`dpop/api-binding` |
| ✓ | `dpop.replay-token-endpoint` The token endpoint rejects a proof whose `jti` it has already accepted within the acceptance window. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L93) | MUST | company | `dpop/replay` |
| – | `dpop.replay-elsewhere` Elsewhere a Company may reject a reused `jti`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L94) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `dpop.nonce` A Company may require proofs to include a nonce it issued. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L95) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `dpop.nonce-support` Personal Agents support DPoP nonces. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L96) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `dpop.errors` A failed proof check returns `invalid_dpop_proof`, or `use_dpop_nonce` with the nonce in `DPoP-Nonce`: as OAuth errors with HTTP 400 at the token endpoint, and with HTTP 401 and the error in `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` at APIs and conversation endpoints. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L97) | MUST | company | `dpop/required` |
| ✓ | `dpop.jkt` Companies support `dpop_jkt` (RFC 9449 §10). _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L98) | MUST | company | `direct/consent-page`<br>`direct/code-exchange` |
| → | `dpop.bind-code` Personal Agents bind the authorization code in Direct Sign-In to the Session Key, with `dpop_jkt` or a proof on a pushed authorization request. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L99) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.mcp-resource` To get a token for an MCP server, the Personal Agent includes `resource` set to the MCP server's `url` from `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L100) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.mcp-dpop` For an MCP server that supports DPoP, a token request with its `resource` gets a DPoP Session Token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L101) | MUST | company | `mcp/dpop-token` |
| ✓ | `tokens.bearer-by-exchange` The Company issues a Personal Agent a Bearer Session Token only by Token Exchange for an MCP server that doesn't support DPoP, and rejects a token exchange for an MCP server that supports DPoP, and any other token request for one that doesn't, with `invalid_target`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L102) | MUST NOT | company | `mcp/no-bearer` |
| → | `tokens.scheme` The Personal Agent uses the scheme that `token_type` names. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L103) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.bearer-one-mcp` Companies accept a Bearer Session Token only at the MCP server whose `url` equals its `resource`, and reject it at every other endpoint, including other paths on the same host. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L104) | MUST | company | `tokens/dpop-outside-mcp` |
| ✓ | `tokens.dpop-elsewhere` Everywhere but an MCP server without DPoP, Companies require DPoP and reject a DPoP Session Token sent with the `Bearer` scheme. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L105) | MUST | company | `mcp/no-bearer`<br>`mcp/resource-bound`<br>`tokens/dpop-outside-mcp` |
| ✓ | `tokens.mcp-should-dpop` New MCP servers support DPoP. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L106) | SHOULD | company | `mcp/dpop-token` |
| ✓ | `tokens.mcp-dpop-es256` An MCP server that supports DPoP lists `ES256` in its `dpop_signing_alg_values_supported` and verifies proofs as this section describes. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L107) | MUST | company | `mcp/dpop-token` |
| ✎ | `tokens.exchange` A Company that lists an MCP server that doesn't support DPoP supports the token exchange grant, checks that the subject token is valid, issued to the same `client_id` and bound to the proof's key, and returns `invalid_grant` for an invalid or expired subject token. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L108) | MUST | company | _applies to a Company that lists an MCP server without DPoP; Poppyseed's MCP server has DPoP, so it answers every token exchange with invalid_target (mcp/no-bearer)_ |
| → | `tokens.narrower` Any token request may include `scope`, to ask for fewer scopes than the Session has, and `resource` (RFC 8707), to ask for a token for one service. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L109) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.resource-bound` A service whose `poppy.json` entry has a `resource`, and every MCP server, accepts a token only if it was issued for its `resource` or `url`; otherwise one DPoP Session Token works at all of a Company's services. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L110) | MUST | company | `mcp/resource-bound`<br>`tokens/dpop-outside-mcp` |
| ✓ | `tokens.no-cookies` Companies accept the token in the `Authorization` header without requiring cookies. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L111) | MUST | company | `mcp/protocol`<br>`apis/openapi` |
| → | `tokens.always-send` Personal Agents send a Session Token on every API and conversation request, and never leave it out to appear to the Company as a person. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L112) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.use-newest` Whenever the Personal Agent gets a new Session Token for a Session, it uses the new token from then on. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L113) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `tokens.not-in-url` Personal Agents do not send tokens in a URL, and Companies do not accept them from one. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L114) | MUST NOT | both | `mcp/token-not-in-url` |
| ✓ | `tokens.rate-limit` A Company that limits request rates returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header when a request goes over the limit, on any endpoint, API, conversation or website, with the body `{"error": "rate_limited"}` at the token endpoint and at endpoints the protocol or an extension defines. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L115) | MUST | company | `mediated/rate-limit`<br>`tokens/rate-limit` |
| → | `tokens.retry-after` On HTTP 429 the Personal Agent waits at least the `Retry-After` time before sending the request again. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sessions.md#L116) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.4 Signing in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `signin.offered` A Company whose issuer supports the authorization code or device grant for other clients offers Direct or Device Sign-In to Personal Agents too. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L15) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in` |
| → | `signin.user-present` A Personal Agent uses direct or Device Sign-In only when the User signs in themselves. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L16) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `signin.revoke-misuse` Companies may revoke the `client_id` of a Personal Agent that uses direct or Device Sign-In without the User signing in themselves. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L17) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `signin.prefer-delegated` A Personal Agent uses Direct or Device Sign-In rather than Mediated Sign-In when the Company offers it and its scopes cover the task. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L18) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✎ | `signin.cover-tasks` A Company that offers Direct or Device Sign-In makes its scopes and APIs cover the tasks Users ask Personal Agents to do. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L19) | SHOULD | company | _a policy each Company sets with its tools and scopes_ |
| ✓ | `signin.scope-namespace` Company scope names do not start with `poppy:`, which is reserved for this protocol. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L20) | MUST NOT | company | `discovery/scopes` |
| → | `signin.scopes-from-metadata` The Personal Agent requests only scopes from `scopes_supported`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L21) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `signin.describe-scopes` The Company describes each scope in `scopes_supported`, in the scopes of an OAuth 2.0 security scheme in an OpenAPI description it lists, or otherwise in `auth.scopes`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L22) | MUST | company | `discovery/scopes` |
| ✓ | `signin.scope-enforcement` Companies decide which operations require each scope and enforce them across web browsing, APIs and actions performed by the Company Agent. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L23) | MUST | company | `signin/partial-approval` |
| ✓ | `signin.grantable` Direct and Device Sign-In can grant any scope in `scopes_supported`, and Mediated Sign-In only the scopes in `auth.mediated.scopes`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L24) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in`<br>`mediated/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `signin.no-extra-scopes` The Company does not grant scopes beyond those requested and allowed for the sign-in type used. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L25) | MUST NOT | company | `signin/partial-approval` |
| → | `signin.scope-param` Each sign-in request includes `scope` as a space-separated string following OAuth scope syntax. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L26) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `signin.invalid-scope` Missing, unknown or unavailable scopes in a sign-in request are rejected with `invalid_scope`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L27) | MUST | company | `signin/invalid-scope` |
| → | `signin.least-scopes` A Personal Agent requests only the scopes the User's tasks need. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L28) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `signin.revoke-old` When the User signs in again for more access, the new Account Token replaces the old one, which the Personal Agent revokes. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L29) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `signin.pending-unchanged` A pending or failed sign-in leaves existing tokens unchanged. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L30) | MUST | company | `device/sign-in`<br>`device/decline` |
| ✓ | `signin.response` Every sign-in type ends with the Account Token in `refresh_token` and a signed-in Session Token for the current Session, with `scope` unless the Company granted exactly the scopes requested, and at least one scope; a sign-in where the User approves none ends as a decline. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L31) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in`<br>`account/refresh`<br>`mediated/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `signin.one-account` A Session is signed in to at most one account, and once it has been it can't switch to another, even after sign-out; the code exchange, device poll or Mediated Sign-In returns `account_mismatch` and issues no tokens. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L32) | MUST | company | `signin/one-account` |
| ✓ | `signin.token-snapshot` Each Session Token reflects the Session as it was when issued, so a request with a signed-out token is handled as signed out and an account action fails with `insufficient_scope`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L33) | MUST | company | `mcp/scope-challenge`<br>`signin/token-snapshot` |
| → | `signin.reuse-account` Before starting a new sign-in, the Personal Agent checks whether it already holds an Account Token that covers the task. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L34) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.5 Direct Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `direct.dpop-jkt` The Personal Agent includes `dpop_jkt` in the authorization URL, or pushes the request with a proof signed with the Session Key. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L40) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `direct.bind-code` The Company binds the code to the Session Key, and at the exchange checks that the proof's key is that key and that its Session belongs to the same `client_id`, returning `invalid_grant` for a proof from a different key. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L41) | MUST | company | `direct/code-exchange` |
| ✓ | `direct.consent` The Company's page shows which Personal Agent is asking, with the name and logo from its metadata, and the requested scopes, and lets the User approve some or all of them, or decline. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L42) | MUST | company | `direct/consent-page`<br>`signin/partial-approval` |
| ✓ | `direct.redirect-iss` The Company redirects to `redirect_uri` with a one-time `code`, the same `state` and its `auth.issuer` in `iss` (RFC 9207), or with `error=access_denied` and `iss` when the User declines. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L43) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in`<br>`direct/decline` |
| ✓ | `direct.redirect-exact` `redirect_uri` exactly matches an entry in the Personal Agent's `redirect_uris`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L44) | MUST | company | `direct/redirect-exact` |
| → | `direct.iss-check` The Personal Agent checks `state`, and checks that `iss` exactly matches the `auth.issuer` of the Company it started sign-in with. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L45) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `direct.exchange` At the code exchange the Company verifies the code, the PKCE verifier and the client assertion, and returns `invalid_grant` for an expired or reused code. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L46) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in`<br>`direct/code-exchange` |

## §4.6 Device Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✎ | `device.rfc10027` Companies that offer Device Sign-In and Personal Agents that use it follow the best practices in RFC 10027 (BCP 247) §2, including using the device authorization grant only when other cross-device flows aren't viable. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L52) | MUST | both | _codes are single-use and expire in 10 minutes by default, polling and wrong codes are limited (device/abuse), and the page names the agent and asks to compare the code (device/sign-in); each Company still assesses its own risk_ |
| → | `device.link-host` Before showing the link and code, the Personal Agent checks that the link's host is the host of `auth.issuer` or of a URL in `protected_resources`, or a subdomain of either, and shows the Company's `organization.name` and domain with them. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `device.open-not-approve` Opening the verification link does not approve the request by itself. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L54) | MUST NOT | company | `device/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `device.consent` The Company's page shows which Personal Agent is asking and the requested scopes, and the User approves some or all of them, or declines. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L55) | MUST | company | `device/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `device.bind-key` The Company binds the `device_code` to the key of the first poll's proof, returns `invalid_grant` to a poll with any other key, and signs in that key's Session once the User approves. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L56) | MUST | company | `device/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `device.polling` Until the User finishes, the token endpoint returns `authorization_pending` or `slow_down`; then the tokens, `access_denied` if the User declined, or `expired_token` after `expires_in`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L57) | MUST | company | `device/sign-in`<br>`device/decline`<br>`device/expired` |

## §4.7 Mediated Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✎ | `mediated.transitional` A Company offers Mediated Sign-In only until it can add Direct or Device Sign-In, and stops once those cover the scopes it grants. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L70) | SHOULD | company | _a policy each Company sets; the config docs mark Mediated Sign-In transitional_ |
| → | `mediated.secret-fields` The Personal Agent protects a value marked `secret`: never shown back to the User, written to logs, or sent anywhere else. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L71) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `mediated.flow` The endpoint answers each status with HTTP 200, a wrong code returns `code_required` until the Company's attempt limit and then `failed`, a code submitted to a `failed` or `expired` sign-in returns that status again, and only the Session that started a sign-in can finish it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L72) | MUST | company | `mediated/sign-in`<br>`mediated/failures`<br>`mediated/code` |
| ✓ | `mediated.errors` Problems with the request are JSON errors: `invalid_scope` (400), `account_mismatch` (400), and `sign_in_not_found` (404) for a `sign_in_id` that is unknown or was started by a different Session. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L73) | MUST | company | `mediated/failures`<br>`mediated/code` |
| ✓ | `mediated.rate-limit` A Company that offers Mediated Sign-In rate-limits attempts. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L74) | MUST | company | `mediated/rate-limit` |
| ✓ | `mediated.no-credentials-returned` A Company that offers Mediated Sign-In does not return credentials in any response. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L75) | MUST NOT | company | `mediated/sign-in`<br>`mediated/failures` |
| ✓ | `mediated.otp-unusual` A Company that offers Mediated Sign-In requires a one-time code when a sign-in looks unusual. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L76) | SHOULD | company | `mediated/code` |
| → | `mediated.endpoint-only` Personal Agents send credentials only to the Company's `auth.mediated.endpoint`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L77) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.by-issuer` A Personal Agent chooses which stored credentials to send by the Company's `auth.issuer`, never by the field labels or the endpoint, and shows the Company's `organization.name` and domain whenever it asks the User for credentials or a code. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L78) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.discard` After a sign-in ends, the Personal Agent discards the credentials or keeps them only in a credential store the User chose, and nowhere else, including model context and logs. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L79) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.no-resign-in` After the User or the Company revokes the Personal Agent's access, it does not sign in again with stored credentials unless the User asks it to. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L80) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.8 Account Tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `account.where-accepted` Companies accept an Account Token only at their `token_endpoint` and `revocation_endpoint`, and only from the `client_id` it was issued to, authenticated by its client assertion. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L86) | MUST | company | `account/refresh` |
| ✓ | `account.session-match` The Session belongs to the same `client_id` and User ID as the Account Token, and has not been signed in to a different account, even if now signed out; otherwise the Company returns `invalid_grant` or `account_mismatch`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L87) | MUST | company | `signin/one-account`<br>`account/session-match` |
| → | `account.narrow` `scope` may ask for fewer scopes than the Account Token has. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L88) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `account.no-widen` A refresh can't ask for more scopes than the Account Token has. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L89) | MUST NOT | company | `account/no-widen` |
| ✓ | `account.lifetime` Using an Account Token doesn't extend its lifetime, and an expired or revoked one returns `invalid_grant` while the Session continues signed out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L90) | MUST | company | `account/refresh`<br>`signout/revoke` |
| – | `account.rotation` A Company may return a new Account Token in `refresh_token`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L91) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `account.use-rotated` When the Company returns a new Account Token, the Personal Agent uses the new one from then on. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L92) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `account.not-key-bound` The Company doesn't bind the Account Token to a Session Key, so one Account Token can start Sessions with different keys. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L93) | MUST | company | `account/refresh` |
| → | `account.secret` Personal Agents store Account Tokens as secrets, and never put them in model context, conversation messages, logs or URLs. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L94) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.9 Signing out

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `signout.revoke` The Company revokes the Account Token and signs out every Session signed in with it, and those Sessions continue signed out, able to sign in again only to the same account. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L100) | MUST | company | `signout/revoke` |
| – | `signout.end-sessions` A Company may end the Sessions at sign-out instead, and renewal then returns `invalid_grant`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L101) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `signout.invalidate-tokens` The Company also invalidates the Session Tokens issued under the same sign-in, as RFC 7009 §2.1 describes. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L102) | SHOULD | company | `signout/revoke` |
| ✓ | `signout.check-per-request` A Company that can't invalidate them checks on each request whether the Session is still signed in. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L103) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/ended-session`<br>`signout/revoke`<br>`web/follows-session` |
| ✎ | `signout.short-lifetimes` A Company that does neither uses much shorter Session Token lifetimes, such as a few minutes. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L104) | SHOULD | company | _Poppyseed invalidates signed-in Session Tokens at sign-out (signout/revoke), so the fallbacks do not apply_ |
| – | `signout.running-work` Work the Company accepted with a valid token can continue after that token expires, and when access is revoked the Company may stop work in progress that uses the account, or let it finish. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L105) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `signout.disconnect` When the User disconnects the Personal Agent in account settings, the Company revokes its Account Tokens for that account and signs out its Sessions. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L106) | MUST | company | `signout/disconnect` |
| ✓ | `signout.after` After sign-out, what doesn't need the account carries on, and anything that used it, such as a conversation or an operation, stays as it is but answers a signed-out token with `insufficient_scope`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L107) | MUST | company | `ops/access`<br>`conv/account-bound` |
| → | `signout.no-resign-in` After sign-out, the Personal Agent does not sign in to that account again unless the User asks, even when a request gets `insufficient_scope`. [↗](pap-0.3/04-sign-in.md#L108) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5 Web browsing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `web.join-before-browse` When a Company lists `web.browser_session_endpoint`, the Personal Agent joins its browser to a Session before browsing the Company's website. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L15) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `web.page` The endpoint answers a GET with an HTML page whose form has a hidden `code` and an empty `proof` field and posts to the endpoint. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L16) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ✓ | `web.code` The code has at least 128 random bits and expires no more than 60 seconds after it is issued. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L17) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ✓ | `web.join-cookie` The Company ties the code to the browser that loaded the page with a cookie set in the same response, which is `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` and uses the `__Host-` prefix. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L18) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ✓ | `web.page-headers` The page is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L19) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ✓ | `web.page-no-effect` Loading the page does not start, end or change any Session, or change the browser's other cookies. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L20) | MUST NOT | company | `web/page` |
| → | `web.proof` The Personal Agent signs a DPoP Proof with the Session Key of the Session the browser joins, with `htm` `POST`, `htu` the endpoint, the code as `nonce` and no `ath`, puts it in the `proof` field and has its browser submit the form. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L21) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.own-code` The Personal Agent takes the code only from the page its own browser loaded from the endpoint, never from anywhere else, and reads it and signs the proof in software its model can't read. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `web.verify` The Company checks that the request has the cookie from the page and it matches `code`, that the code is one it issued, unexpired and unused, with a code used by the first request that sends it whatever the result, that `proof` is a valid DPoP Proof for this request with the code as `nonce`, and that its key is the Session Key of an active Session. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L23) | MUST | company | `web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.response` When every check passes, the Company sets its cookie for the Session, clears the page's cookie and responds `303 See Other` to a page on its website; otherwise it sets no cookie and returns an error page with HTTP 400, or 429 for too many requests. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L24) | MUST | company | `web/join`<br>`web/verify` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-set-once` The Session's cookie is set only in that response. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L25) | MUST | company | `web/join` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-follows-session` The cookie follows the Session's current state, so when the Session signs in or out or its scopes change, the website reflects it on the next request. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L26) | MUST | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-lifetime` The cookie does not outlive the Session. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L27) | MUST NOT | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-flags` The cookie is `Secure` and `HttpOnly`. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L28) | MUST | company | `web/join` |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-host-prefix` The cookie uses the `__Host-` prefix, unless it has to cover several hosts. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L29) | SHOULD | company | `web/join` |
| ✓ | `web.scopes` The website applies the Session's scopes, and while the browser carries the Session's cookie the Company handles its requests as that Session, whatever other cookies the browser holds. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L30) | MUST | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ✎ | `web.missing-scope` When the website refuses an action because the Session lacks a scope, it shows a visible error message that names the missing scopes. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L31) | SHOULD | company | _the Company's own pages; browserSession() gives them the Session's scopes, and the reference company's /account names the scope it needs_ |
| → | `web.rejoin` The Personal Agent may join again at any time, and each join replaces the cookie the Company set before. [↗](pap-0.3/05-web.md#L32) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 APIs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `apis.types` Each API's `type` is `openapi` or `mcp`. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L22) | MUST | company | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| ✓ | `apis.openapi-description` An `openapi` entry's `url` points to an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 description of the API. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L23) | MUST | company | `apis/openapi` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-transport` An `mcp` entry's `url` is a remote MCP server endpoint using the Streamable HTTP transport and MCP version 2025-06-18 or later. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L24) | MUST | company | `mcp/protocol` |
| → | `apis.skip-unknown` Personal Agents skip API types they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L25) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `apis.session-tokens` Every listed API accepts Session Tokens as described in 4.3: DPoP for OpenAPI, and for MCP, DPoP if the server supports it and Bearer if it doesn't. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L26) | MUST | company | `apis/openapi` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-scopes` A listed MCP server accepts Session Tokens as its access tokens and enforces their scopes. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L27) | MUST | company | `mcp/public-tool`<br>`mcp/scope-challenge` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-resource` A listed MCP server accepts only tokens issued for its `url`. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L28) | MUST | company | `mcp/resource-bound` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-metadata` The MCP server's protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) lists `auth.issuer` in `authorization_servers`. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L29) | MUST | company | `mcp/challenge` |
| – | `apis.mcp-clients` An MCP client that doesn't implement this protocol may sign in with MCP's own authorization flow, which starts a signed-in Session with no User ID that ends when its sign-in is revoked or expires. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L30) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `apis.errors` Token failures at APIs return `invalid_token` (401), `invalid_dpop_proof` or `use_dpop_nonce` (401), `insufficient_scope` (403, naming the scopes in `scope`) or `extension_required` (403) in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L31) | MUST | company | `mcp/challenge`<br>`mcp/scope-challenge` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-challenges` An MCP server's 401 responses carry a challenge for each scheme it accepts, each with `resource_metadata` naming its protected resource metadata URL. [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L32) | MUST | company | `mcp/challenge` |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-extension-required` An MCP server returns `extension_required` only to refuse the Personal Agent entirely, never for one tool. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/06-apis.md#L33) | MUST | company | `ops/require-extension` |

## §7.1 Conversation protocols

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.protocol-choice` The Personal Agent chooses a protocol it supports from `agent.protocols`, uses that entry's endpoint, and skips unfamiliar types. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L9) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.2 Requests

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.session-token` Every conversation request carries a Session Token with a DPoP Proof. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L21) | MUST | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.isolation` A conversation belongs to the `client_id` and User ID that started it, and to the account once it uses one; the Company rejects requests from any other `client_id`, User or account. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L22) | MUST | company | `conv/isolation`<br>`conv/account-bound` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-format` Conversation, message and event IDs are strings of 1 to 256 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L23) | MUST | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-prefix` IDs start with a short prefix for their kind, such as `cnv_`, `msg_` or `evt_`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L24) | SHOULD | both | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.id-opaque` Beyond the format rules, the side that doesn't choose an ID does not depend on its format. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L25) | MUST NOT | both | `conv/start` |

## §7.3 Sending messages

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.start` Starting a conversation returns HTTP 201 with `conversation_id`, `status` and `responder`, and later messages to `{id}/messages` return HTTP 202 with the same fields. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L29) | MUST | company | `conv/start` |
| → | `conv.message-id-unique` The Personal Agent makes each message `id` unique for the User, and retries a message with the same ID. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L30) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.message-idempotent` A message with an already accepted ID and the same content returns the original response without adding it again, including a retried first message; different content returns `message_id_conflict`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L31) | MUST | company | `conv/message-idempotent` |
| ✓ | `conv.wait` With the `wait` query parameter (and optionally `cursor`) on either POST, the Company accepts the message, then responds as a read of the events from that cursor would, holding the request up to `wait` seconds, with status 201 or 202. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L32) | MUST | company | `conv/reply` |

## §7.4 Message fields

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.message-content` A message has at least one of `text`, `data` or `context`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L45) | MUST | both | `conv/message-content` |
| ✓ | `conv.text-plain` Personal Agents and Company Agents do not put JSON or other markup in `text`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L46) | SHOULD NOT | both | `conv/reply` |
| → | `conv.context-formats` When the Personal Agent shares `locale`, `time_zone` or `user_available`, it uses those fields and their formats: an RFC 5646 language tag, an IANA time zone name, and a boolean. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L47) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conv.context-extra` `context` may include other fields. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L48) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `conv.context-ignore` A Company may ignore `context` fields beyond those defined. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L49) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conv.context-minimal` Personal Agents share only what the task needs. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L50) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.role` The Company sets each recorded message's `role` to `user` or `company` for the side it came from, and ignores a `role` the Personal Agent sends. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L51) | MUST | company | `conv/message-content` |
| ✓ | `conv.context-sticky` `context` fields a message leaves out keep their previous values, and only the Personal Agent sends `context`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L52) | MUST | company | `conv/context-sticky` |

## §7.5 Reading events

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.skip-unknown-events` Personal Agents skip event types they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L58) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conv.cursor-opaque` Cursors are opaque, and the Personal Agent does not compare or sort them. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L59) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.events` Each event's `id` is also a cursor, a read without `cursor` starts at the beginning, a read that times out returns an empty `events` list, and every message the Company accepts is recorded as it was sent, including one with only `context`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L60) | MUST | company | `conv/start`<br>`conv/cursors` |
| – | `conv.wait-cap` The Company may return a read before `wait` elapses, or cap `wait`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L61) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `conv.wait-cap-held` A `wait` larger than the Company's cap is held for the cap, not rejected, and `wait` is a whole number of seconds, 0 or more. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L62) | MUST | company | `conv/cursors` |
| ✓ | `conv.read-fields` Every successful read includes `conversation_id`, `events`, `cursor`, `has_more`, `status` and `responder`, with `events` empty when there are none; `cursor` is the last event returned, or the request's cursor if there were none. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L63) | MUST | company | `conv/start`<br>`conv/cursors` |
| ✓ | `conv.cursor-expired-error` A cursor for events the Company no longer has returns `cursor_expired`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L64) | MUST | company | `conv/cursor-expired` |
| → | `conv.cursor-expired` On `cursor_expired` the Personal Agent reads from the beginning and tells the User that part of the conversation is missing. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L65) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.6 Streaming

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conv.sse` A Company may stream events with server-sent events when a read sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, with each event's ID as the SSE `id` and the event JSON as `data`; one that doesn't stream returns JSON. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L69) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `conv.sse-close` A Company may close a stream at any time, and the Personal Agent reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L70) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `conv.last-event-id` When a request has both `Last-Event-ID` and `cursor`, `Last-Event-ID` wins. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L71) | MUST | company | `conv/stream` |
| – | `conv.text-delta` While the Company Agent writes a message, the Company may send pieces of its text as `text-delta` events with no SSE `id`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L72) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conv.text-delta-ignore` The Personal Agent does not act on text from a `text-delta` event. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L73) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.7 Status and responder

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.status-responder` Every successful response to a POST or a read includes `status` and `responder`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L79) | MUST | company | `conv/start` |
| ✓ | `conv.state-events` Every change to `status` or `responder` adds a `state` event with both. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L80) | MUST | company | `conv/reply`<br>`conv/handoff` |
| ✓ | `conv.company-sender` Each Company message includes `sender`, `agent` or `human`, and its `role` stays `company`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L81) | MUST | company | `conv/reply`<br>`conv/handoff` |

## §7.8 Human or AI

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conv.agent-sender` The Personal Agent sets each message's `sender` to `agent` when it wrote the message, and to `human` only when the message carries the User's own words. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L85) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7.9 Handoff to a person

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.handoff` A handoff request with an empty JSON object returns HTTP 202 with `status` and `responder`; the status becomes `queued`, `responder` becomes `human` when a person joins, and if no one is available the status returns to `idle` with a message saying why; a handoff to a conversation already `queued` or with a person returns HTTP 202 with the current state and changes nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L89) | MUST | company | `conv/handoff` |

## §7.10 Direct Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.direct` The parent of a Direct Conversation is open, belongs to the same owner, is not itself a Direct Conversation, and has at most one open Direct Conversation; otherwise the Company returns `conversation_not_found`, `conversation_closed` or `direct_conversation_open`. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L93) | MUST | company | `conv/direct` |
| ✓ | `conv.direct-parent` Opening and closing a Direct Conversation adds `direct_opened` and `direct_closed` events to the parent, the parent refuses messages and handoff with `direct_conversation_open` while it is open, and closing the parent closes its open Direct Conversation. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L94) | MUST | company | `conv/direct` |
| ✎ | `conv.user-requested` A `user_requested` event, with a short `reason`, doesn't change `status` or `responder`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L95) | MUST | company | _AgentTurn.askForUser appends the event and nothing else (packages/core/src/conversations.ts); the scripted reference Company Agent doesn't ask for the User_ |

## §7.11 Sign-in during a conversation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.authorization-message` When the Company adds an `authorization` event, it also asks in a message. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L99) | SHOULD | company | `conv/sign-in` |
| → | `conv.token-switch` The Personal Agent may switch to a new Session Token partway through a conversation, or continue it in a new Session, as long as the token matches the conversation's owner. [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L100) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `conv.scopes` Before reading account information or making a change, the Company Agent checks for the required scopes, whoever is handling the conversation, and sending a message does not authorize an account action. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L101) | MUST | company | `conv/scopes` |
| ✓ | `conv.authorization-event` When the Company Agent needs the User's account or more scopes, the Company adds an `authorization` event with `error` `insufficient_scope` and the needed `scope`, and the conversation stays open. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L102) | MUST | company | `conv/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `conv.account-bound` Once a conversation has used the User's account, a request on it from a token for the same User that isn't signed in to that account gets `insufficient_scope`, and after a sign-out the conversation stays open. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L103) | MUST | company | `conv/account-bound` |

## §7.12 Closing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.close` Closing with an empty JSON object adds a `state` event with `status: "closed"`, cancels any pending handoff and returns HTTP 200 with `status` and `responder`; closing a closed conversation returns the same response and adds no event; a closed conversation takes no more messages and its events stay readable. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L107) | MUST | company | `conv/close`<br>`conv/handoff` |

## §7.13 Errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `conv.errors` Non-token errors have a JSON body with an `error` code and the statuses above, and an unknown Conversation ID and one belonging to someone else return the same `conversation_not_found`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/07-conversations.md#L123) | MUST | company | `conv/message-idempotent`<br>`conv/cursors`<br>`conv/isolation`<br>`conv/close` |

## §8.1 Excluded tasks

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `tasks.document` `excluded_tasks.url` serves a JSON document with `tasks`, each with a `task` phrase of at most 200 characters and an optional `alternative`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L15) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| ✎ | `tasks.not-offered` A listed task isn't offered through any of the Company's interfaces: its Company Agent, its APIs, or its website in a browser session. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L16) | MUST | company | _the Company keeps the tasks it lists in excludedTasks out of its tools and Company Agent_ |
| ✓ | `tasks.public` The document is the same for every User, and is fetched with a GET and no token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L17) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| → | `tasks.cache` The Personal Agent caches the document according to its HTTP caching headers. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L18) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.read-first` A Personal Agent reads the document before it starts on a task at the Company. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L19) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skip-unknown` Personal Agents skip fields they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L20) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.2 Alternatives

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `tasks.alternative` An alternative has at least one of `instructions`, at most 2,000 characters, or `references`, each with a `type` and that type's fields. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L30) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| ✓ | `tasks.listed-apis` An `openapi` or `mcp` reference names an API listed in the Company's `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L31) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| → | `tasks.ignore-unlisted` Personal Agents ignore an `openapi` or `mcp` reference that doesn't name a listed API, and skip reference types they don't recognize. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L32) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.alternative-is-content` An alternative is content from the Company, and its `instructions` are not instructions the Personal Agent has to follow. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L33) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.3 Feedback

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `feedback.send` When a User's task can't be done through the protocol, the Personal Agent may send a report to `feedback.endpoint`. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L39) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `feedback.session-token` A Company accepts a report only with a Session Token, signed in or signed out, and needs no scope for it. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L40) | MUST | company | `tasks/feedback` |
| → | `feedback.kind` Personal Agents send only the `kind` `missing`, with a `task` of at most 200 characters and a `description` of at most 2,000 characters. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L41) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.no-personal-data` Personal Agents don't put personal data in a report, such as the User's name, contact details or order details. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L42) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.no-secrets` Personal Agents don't put secrets in a report. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L43) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.once` A Personal Agent sends one report for each task it couldn't do, not one for each attempt. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L44) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `feedback.not-excluded` A Personal Agent does not report a task the Company lists as excluded. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L45) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `feedback.unknown-kind` A Company accepts a `kind` it doesn't recognize. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L46) | MUST | company | `tasks/feedback` |
| ✎ | `feedback.as-data` Companies treat a report's text as data, not as instructions, including when a model reads it. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L47) | MUST | company | _reports go to the Company's feedback handler as data and never to a model; the FeedbackReport docs say so_ |
| ✓ | `feedback.response` The Company responds with HTTP 202 and no body, or HTTP 200 with an alternative when the task can be done after all; other errors are JSON, `invalid_request` (400) for a report that is malformed or too long and `rate_limited` (429). _(implied)_ [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L48) | MUST | company | `tasks/feedback` |
| → | `feedback.accept-either` Personal Agents accept either response. [↗](pap-0.3/08-tasks.md#L49) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.secrets-out-of-model` Personal Agents keep Session Tokens, Account Tokens, private keys, authorization codes, PKCE code verifiers and device codes out of model context. [↗](pap-0.3/09-security.md#L13) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 3 Operations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
